scope: Proposition 2.4 (Weak-equivalence test) of the manuscript “The Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis via elementary expansions” (preprints/The-Grothendieck-homotopy-hypothesis-via-elementary-expansions-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 312 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 489bb8f5a448c3fc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 7-8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For a model map f : X → Y , the following are equivalent. 1. f ∈ W. 2. It induces a bijection on π0 and a bijection πr(X; u, v) −→ πr(Y ; fu, fv) for every r ≥ 1 and every parallel pair u, v in X. 7 3. For every r ≥ 0, every specified boundary b : ∂Dr → X, and every r-cell y of Y with boundary fb, there are an r-cell x with boundary exactly b and an (r + 1)-cell fx → y in Y . In particular, a weak equivalence reflects homotopy between parallel cells, including equality of components for vertices.
